sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯汀·

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话实况。

sentences.zh: 我们将在11月18日通过nytimes.com免费直播部分精选采访，供所有人观看。

If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻报道的一个月免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily One.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》第一期。

sentences.en: Today, the city of Charlottesville, Virginia is transformed into a battleground in one of the bloodiest fights yet over the removal of Confederate monuments across the South.
sentences.zh: 今天，弗吉尼亚州夏洛茨维尔市变成了一个战场，这里正在上演南方各地移除邦联纪念碑以来最血腥的冲突之一。

sentences.en: And the president condemns the violence, quote, on all sides, but does not take special aim at the white nationalists.
sentences.zh: 总统谴责了“各方”的暴力行为，但并没有特别针对白人民族主义者。

sentences.en: It's Monday, August 14th.
sentences.zh: 今天是8月14日，星期一。

sentences.en: Cheryl Gay Stolberg, you were there in Charlottesville this weekend as all these events unfolded.
sentences.zh: 谢丽尔·盖伊·斯托尔伯格，这个周末当所有这些事件发生时，你就在夏洛茨维尔现场。
zh_words: 谢丽尔·盖伊·斯托尔伯格

sentences.en: Start us at the beginning.
sentences.zh: 请从头开始讲起。

sentences.en: What was supposed to be happening this weekend?
sentences.zh: 这个周末原本计划发生什么？

sentences.en: Well, what was supposed to be happening was a noon rally, so-called Unite the Right rally, hosted by white nationalists at Emancipation Park, formerly called Lee Park.
sentences.zh: 嗯，原本计划在中午举行一场集会，即所谓的“团结右翼”集会，由白人民族主义者在解放公园（原名李公园）主办。

sentences.en: Emancipation Park has a statue of General Robert E.
sentences.zh: 解放公园中间有一座罗伯特·E·

sentences.en: Lee in the middle of it, a statue of him riding a horse.
sentences.zh: 李将军的雕像，是他骑马的雕像。

sentences.en: The city wants to remove the statue, and white nationalists are protesting the removal.
sentences.zh: 市政府想要移除这座雕像，而白人民族主义者正在抗议这种移除行为。

sentences.en: So what actually happens this weekend?
sentences.zh: 那么这个周末实际上发生了什么？

sentences.en: Start us, Cheryl, with Friday night.
sentences.zh: 谢丽尔，请从周五晚上开始讲起。

sentences.en: So Friday night, after dark, a band of these white nationalists came onto the University of
sentences.zh: 周五晚上天黑后，一群白人民族主义者来到弗吉尼亚大学

sentences.en: Virginia campus, carrying torches, and they were chanting,
sentences.zh: 校园，他们举着火把，高呼着：

sentences.en: you will not replace us, Jews will not replace us.
sentences.zh: “你们不会取代我们，犹太人不会取代我们。”

sentences.en: This is just such an intimidating
sentences.zh: 这真是一个令人胆寒的

sentences.en: moment, Michael.
sentences.zh: 时刻，迈克尔。

sentences.en: I mean, the torch at night in here in the South just evokes memories of the KKK, and there was a scuffle there, there were some arrests, a police officer was injured,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在南方的夜晚，火把让人联想到三K党，当时发生了一些冲突，有人被捕，一名警察受伤，

sentences.en: and that was kind of the precursor to the events of Saturday.
sentences.zh: 那算是周六事件的前奏。

sentences.en: So let's talk about Saturday.
sentences.zh: 那我们来谈谈周六吧。

sentences.en: There was, at 6 a.m., a sunrise service at the First Baptist Church here, a historically black church,
sentences.zh: 早上6点，这里的第一浸信会教堂举行了一场日出礼拜，这是一座历史悠久的黑人教堂，

sentences.en: where faith leaders and people who wanted to come out and demonstrate against these alt-right protesters gathered.
sentences.zh: 信仰领袖和那些想要出来抗议这些极右翼抗议者的人们聚集在那里。

sentences.en: How sweet it is to be in the struggle for justice.
sentences.zh: 为正义而奋斗是多么美好啊。

sentences.en: They heard from Dr. Cornel West, Harvard Divinity professor and political activist, who told me he was coming to bear witness to the face of white supremacy.
sentences.zh: 他们听取了哈佛神学院教授、政治活动家康奈尔·韦斯特博士的发言，他告诉我，他来这里是为了见证白人至上主义者的真面目。

sentences.en: And then across town at around 9 o'clock in the morning, the alt-right white nationalists,
sentences.zh: 然后，大约早上9点，在城另一边的麦金太尔公园，极右翼白人民族主义者、

sentences.en: neo-Nazi, white supremacists, were gathering in a different park, a park called McIntyre Park.
sentences.zh: 新纳粹分子和白人至上主义者聚集在另一个公园。

sentences.en: Now, their rally was not supposed to start until noon, but they were pulled up in their cars and
sentences.zh: 他们的集会本应在中午才开始，但他们开着车和

sentences.en: their trucks with their flags and some carrying shields, some wearing helmets, you know, just getting ready for battle.
sentences.zh: 卡车赶到，带着旗帜，有些人带着盾牌，有些人戴着头盔，你知道，就是为了战斗做准备。

sentences.en: Let's see what I'm talking about.
sentences.zh: 让我们看看我在说什么。

sentences.en: Look at these burly, strong, proud, white boys.
sentences.zh: 看看这些魁梧、强壮、骄傲的白人小伙子们。

sentences.en: And they were going to head downtown to Emancipation Park.
sentences.zh: 他们正准备前往市中心的解放公园。

sentences.en: Now, mind you, their rally was not supposed to start until noon, but everything was getting going a lot earlier than expected.
sentences.zh: 请注意，他们的集会本应在中午才开始，但一切都比预期的要早得多。

sentences.en: So you had on the one end of the city, the people at church, which consisted of a lot of members of the clergy, about 30, and others.
sentences.zh: 所以，在城市的一端，教堂里的人们，包括大约30名神职人员和其他人，

sentences.en: They had trained in the tactics of nonviolent proteSt. They were prepared to be arrested or to get involved in violence.
sentences.zh: 他们受过非暴力抗议策略的训练。他们做好了被捕或卷入暴力的准备。

sentences.en: They were marching to Emancipation Park.
sentences.zh: 他们正向解放公园进发。

sentences.en: And so what you had was these two groups converging on this park where the statue was.
sentences.zh: 所以，你看到的是这两群人汇聚在这个有雕像的公园。

sentences.en: And clearly to confront each other.
sentences.zh: 显然是为了相互对抗。

sentences.en: Clearly.
sentences.zh: 显而易见。

sentences.en: Now, the whole park was surrounded with police barricades and police tape.
sentences.zh: 现在，整个公园都被警察的路障和警戒线包围了。

sentences.en: And inside the barricades was a line of Virginia State Police and Charlottesville Police.
sentences.zh: 路障里面是一排弗吉尼亚州警察和夏洛茨维尔警察。

sentences.en: And what wound up happening was the alt-right people were funneling their way into the park, the counter-protesters,
sentences.zh: 最终发生的情况是，极右翼分子涌入公园，而反抗议者，

sentences.en: including some dressed in black with helmets and shields, the so-called Antifa, the anti-fascists, were on the outside of the park in the street, on a street called Market Street.
sentences.zh: 包括一些身穿黑衣、戴着头盔和盾牌的所谓“反法西斯主义者”（Antifa），则在公园外的街道上，也就是市场街上。

sentences.en: And so you started to have little skirmishes.
sentences.zh: 于是开始出现了一些小规模冲突。

sentences.en: I was outside the park on Market Street watching as these white supremacists tried to make their way into the park.
sentences.zh: 我当时在公园外的市场街上，看着这些白人至上主义者试图进入公园。

sentences.en: And the counter-demonstrators, including the clergy, were trying to block them.
sentences.zh: 而包括神职人员在内的反抗议者试图阻挡他们。

sentences.en: The clergy also linked arms outside the park, linking arms and singing spirituals, singing, you know, this little light of mine.
sentences.zh: 神职人员也在公园外挽起手臂，一边挽着手臂一边唱着灵歌，唱着《这盏小灯》（This Little Light of Mine）。

sentences.en: I'm going to let it shine.
sentences.zh: 我要让它闪耀。

sentences.en: Just praying and trying to be peaceful, but also trying at certain points to block the entry of the white nationalists.
sentences.zh: 只是在祈祷，试图保持和平，但在某些时刻也试图阻挡白人民族主义者的进入。

sentences.en: And the skirmishes kept getting worse and more intense.
sentences.zh: 冲突变得越来越严重，越来越激烈。

sentences.en: It really felt like the violence was escalating as more and more of these white nationalists kept arriving and people were trying to block them.
sentences.zh: 随着越来越多的白人民族主义者不断赶到，人们试图阻挡他们，暴力事件确实在升级。

sentences.en: Suddenly clubs were coming out and pepper spray was being sprayed and there were smoke bombs being thrown.
sentences.zh: 突然间，棍棒出现了，胡椒喷雾被喷洒，还有烟雾弹被投掷。

sentences.en: And both sides had bats and were beating each other and they were holding up their shields.
sentences.zh: 双方都拿着球棒互相殴打，他们举着盾牌。

sentences.en: And, you know, it was truly a melee.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那真是一场混战。

sentences.en: And at about 11.22, in fact, at precisely 11.22, the governor declared a state of emergency.
sentences.zh: 大约在11点22分，事实上，就在11点22分，州长宣布进入紧急状态。

sentences.en: Virginia's governor, Terry McAuliffe, declaring a state of emergency.
sentences.zh: 弗吉尼亚州州长特里·麦考利夫宣布进入紧急状态。

sentences.en: The crowd ordered to disperse.
sentences.zh: 人群被命令散开。

sentences.en: You're going to leave the area now.
sentences.zh: 你们现在必须离开这个区域。

sentences.en: Everyone asks, how in the world did we get here?
sentences.zh: 每个人都在问，我们到底是怎么走到这一步的？

sentences.en: That is a good question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个好问题。

sentences.en: Cheryl, who were these white nationalist protesters and where did they come from?
sentences.zh: 谢丽尔，这些白人民族主义抗议者是谁？他们从哪里来？

sentences.en: You know, frankly, Michael, it was really hard to find out exactly who they were.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，迈克尔，真的很难查清楚他们到底是谁。

sentences.en: A lot of them wouldn't give me their last names.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人拒绝告诉我他们的姓氏。

sentences.en: One of them gave his name as, I think, Ted from Missouri.
sentences.zh: 其中一个人告诉我他叫泰德，来自密苏里州。

sentences.en: And I said, why won't you give me your last name?
sentences.zh: 我问他，为什么不告诉我你的姓氏？

sentences.en: And he said, I might want to run for public office one day.
sentences.zh: 他说，我以后可能想竞选公职。

sentences.en: And he told me, I'm tired of seeing white people pushed around.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我，我厌倦了看到白人被欺负。

sentences.en: But it's clear that they were coming mostly from out of town and some from in town.
sentences.zh: 但很明显，他们大多是从外地来的，也有一些是本地人。

sentences.en: And interestingly, Michael, a lot of
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，迈克尔，很多

sentences.en: young millennial men, not surprising that they were men, but the age was surprising to me.
sentences.zh: 年轻的千禧一代男性，他们是男性并不奇怪，但年龄让我感到惊讶。

sentences.en: So many young people.
sentences.zh: 这么多年轻人。

sentences.en: When you say young people, you're talking, what, like 20?
sentences.zh: 当你说是年轻人时，你是说，大概20岁左右？

sentences.en: 20s-ish, 30-ish, you know, not middle-aged, but on the younger side.
sentences.zh: 20多岁，30多岁，你知道，不是中年人，而是偏年轻的一代。

sentences.en: So after the crowd dispersed, you know, it was in the downtown area.
sentences.zh: 所以人群散去后，你知道，是在市中心区域。

sentences.en: And there's a downtown pedestrian mall right nearby.
sentences.zh: 附近有一个市中心步行街。

sentences.en: And, you know, there were still lots and lots of protesters, thousands of people wandering around downtown.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，仍然有大量的抗议者，成千上万的人在市中心游荡。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden, seemingly out of nowhere, this gray Dodge Charger starts zooming into the crowd.
sentences.zh: 突然间，似乎凭空出现了一辆灰色道奇Charger，开始冲向人群。

sentences.en: And people are screaming and bodies were flying up in the air.
sentences.zh: 人们在尖叫，身体被撞飞到空中。

sentences.en: And he backed up and rammed another car.
sentences.zh: 然后他倒车，又撞向了另一辆车。

sentences.en: And I was told by eyewitnesses, backed his way out of the street.
sentences.zh: 目击者告诉我，他倒车退出了街道。

sentences.en: There was blood everywhere and glass everywhere.
sentences.zh: 到处都是血，到处都是玻璃。

sentences.en: And it was just a horrific, horrific scene.
sentences.zh: 那真是一个可怕、可怕的场景。

sentences.en: And as we know, a 32-year-old woman, Heather Heyer, who was among the counter-protesters, was killed by that car.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所知，一名32岁的女性希瑟·海耶，她是反抗议者之一，被那辆车撞死了。

sentences.en: And that driver, a man from Ohio, 20-year-old from Ohio, is facing murder charges now.
sentences.zh: 而那个司机，一个来自俄亥俄州的20岁男子，现在面临谋杀指控。

sentences.en: And what do we know about the man who drove into the protesters?
sentences.zh: 关于那个开车冲进抗议者的人，我们知道些什么？

sentences.en: Well, we know a few things about him.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们对他了解一些情况。

sentences.en: We know that he had told his mother that he was coming to Virginia.
sentences.zh: 我们知道他曾告诉母亲他要来弗吉尼亚州。

sentences.en: And I believe she told the local newspaper, the Toledo Blade, that she thought it was somehow related to President Trump.
sentences.zh: 我相信她告诉当地报纸《托莱多刀锋报》，她认为这可能与特朗普总统有关。

sentences.en: At 4.54 Saturday afternoon, Virginia State Police were notified of a helicopter crash in Albemarle County.
sentences.zh: 周六下午4点54分，弗吉尼亚州警方接到通知，阿尔伯马尔县发生了一起直升机坠毁事故。

sentences.en: As if the events of Saturday weren't tragic enough at the end of the day.
sentences.zh: 就好像周六发生的事件在一天结束时还不够悲惨一样。

sentences.en: They located the wreckage of a helicopter.
sentences.zh: 他们发现了直升机的残骸。

sentences.en: A Virginia State Police helicopter crashed, killing two of the troopers inside.
sentences.zh: 一架弗吉尼亚州警方的直升机坠毁，机上的两名警官遇难。

sentences.en: So a tragic, tragic end to a very, very difficult day.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是非常、非常艰难的一天，以一个非常、非常悲惨的结局告终。

sentences.en: And they were responding to this?
sentences.zh: 他们当时是在应对这件事吗？

sentences.en: They were monitoring the situation.
sentences.zh: 他们当时在监控局势。

sentences.en: They were part of the police response.
sentences.zh: 他们是警方应对行动的一部分。

sentences.en: So in the end, we have three deaths here.
sentences.zh: 所以最终，我们这里有三起死亡事件。

sentences.en: Yes, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Three deaths.
sentences.zh: 三起死亡事件。

sentences.en: Cheryl, tell us about the role of the police in all this.
sentences.zh: 谢丽尔，告诉我们警方在这一切中扮演的角色。

sentences.en: Well, the role of the police is a matter of some question here, Michael.
sentences.zh: 嗯，警方扮演的角色在这里是一个值得质疑的问题，迈克尔。

sentences.en: I'm trying to sort that out.
sentences.zh: 我正在努力理清这一点。

sentences.en: I talked to Governor Terry McAuliffe, and also I talked to his Secretary for Public Safety, and they both maintain that the police did exactly as they should have.
sentences.zh: 我采访了州长特里·麦考利夫，也采访了他的公共安全秘书，他们都坚持认为警方做得完全正确。

sentences.en: And they both mentioned that this was a heavily armed crowd.
sentences.zh: 他们都提到这是一群全副武装的人。

sentences.en: And I should have mentioned this to you, Michael.
sentences.zh: 我本该告诉你的，迈克尔。

sentences.en: Along with the line of clergy, there was a line of self-styled militia men carrying assault rifles and wearing camouflage.
sentences.zh: 在神职人员队伍旁边，还有一排自称民兵的人，他们携带突击步枪，身穿迷彩服。

sentences.en: And they looked like, I thought they were the National Guard at firSt. I kept saying, are you the National Guard?
sentences.zh: 起初我以为他们是国民警卫队。我一直在问，你们是国民警卫队吗？

sentences.en: Like, who are you?
sentences.zh: 就像，你们是谁？

sentences.en: Who are they?
sentences.zh: 他们是谁？

sentences.en: And then I could see some of them had patches that said, like, New York militia.
sentences.zh: 然后我看到他们中的一些人有写着“纽约民兵”之类的臂章。

sentences.en: And they would say, well, ma'am, we're just here to keep the peace.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，夫人，我们只是来维持和平的。

sentences.en: We're neutral.
sentences.zh: 我们是中立的。

sentences.en: But nonetheless, it looked like an invading army.
sentences.zh: 但尽管如此，它看起来像一支入侵的军队。

sentences.en: So with all these guns, you know, Virginia is an open carry state.
sentences.zh: 所以带着这么多枪支，你知道，弗吉尼亚州是一个允许公开携带枪支的州。

sentences.en: And with all this violence, both Terry McAuliffe and Brian Moran, the Public Safety
sentences.zh: 面对所有这些暴力事件，特里·麦考利夫和公共安全秘书布莱恩·莫兰

sentences.en: Secretary, told me that they felt it went extremely well, that you could not predict that this car would
sentences.zh: 都告诉我，他们觉得情况处理得非常好，你无法预料到这辆车会

sentences.en: crash into a crowd and kill a woman, that that could not have been predicted or averted.
sentences.zh: 冲进人群撞死一名女性，那是无法预料或避免的。

sentences.en: But I think we're going to be having questions about how the police handled this for a long time to come.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，关于警方如何处理这件事，我们将在很长一段时间内提出疑问。

sentences.en: It sounds like what you're saying, Cheryl, is that with so many armed people on the ground there,
sentences.zh: 听起来你的意思是，谢丽尔，由于现场有这么多武装人员，

sentences.en: that the authorities, law enforcement, is saying that things went pretty well from their perspective, reasonably.
sentences.zh: 当局和执法部门认为从他们的角度来看，事情进展得相当顺利，合情合理。

sentences.en: That is what they're saying.
sentences.zh: 他们确实是这么说的。
